intended_object: The change-of-rings homomorphism K₀(R) → K₀(S) induced by a unital ring homomorphism φ : R → S, sending [P] to [P ⊗_R S] (Weibel, K-book, Ch. II). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
In this library, K0 R is the Grothendieck group (`Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup`) of the monoid `ProjectiveClass R`. That monoid consists of isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective right R-modules, with direct sum as addition. `ProjectiveClass.map φ` is obtained by descending the functor X ↦ X ⊗_R S to classes, using a balanced tensor product with S viewed as an R-module through φ. The descent is justified because this functor preserves isomorphisms, the zero module and binary direct sums. `K0.map φ` is then the universal extension of the composite ProjectiveClass R → ProjectiveClass S → K0 S to the group completion. On generators it gives [P] ↦ [P ⊗_R S] (see `map_ofClass` and `map_of`). This is exactly the standard induced map on K₀.

It is stated for arbitrary (possibly noncommutative) unital rings, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has no algebraic K₀ of rings, so there is no counterpart. Using right modules instead of left modules is a harmless convention.
